A_general.open_code_note: No public Gong MCP server repository or package was found in the prepared source set. The hosted endpoint returned HTTP 401 without authorization; its deployed implementation could not be inspected.
other_official_servers: Gong documents a separate MCP client that connects Gong AI agents to external MCP servers; it is a distinct feature, not another endpoint for this hosted server. https://help.gong.io/docs/about-gong-mcp

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Gong says the server is available on any Gong plan, but connecting users need a paid Gong seat and sufficient Gong credits. MCP queries that analyze calls and emails consume credits; no separate MCP price is published.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Gong does not publish fixed prices on its pricing page; licenses are priced per user and there is a platform fee based on supported users. Pricing is customized.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Credit consumption depends on analyzed data volume and, for briefs, the number of open-ended sections. Repeated requests can analyze the same conversations again and consume credits again. No MCP-specific fixed fee or per-call amount was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: A Gong tech admin creates the integration. Collaborators cannot connect; users need a paid Gong seat. The admin chooses manual or automatic registration and personal or shared authorization context. Client redirect URIs are configured for integrations. Personal access follows the authorizing user's Gong permissions; shared access provides organization-wide data access. Admins can disable or delete integrations, revoking their active tokens.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Gong tech admin controls integration registration, authorization context, redirect URIs, scopes and enablement; Gong controls seat and credit requirements; personal access is also limited by the user's Gong permissions.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official docs describe all three tools as read-only; no tool annotations were published. 2. No server-enforced confirmation flow is documented. 3. OAuth metadata advertises mcp:read and mcp:write; docs say the MCP integration is read-only. Personal context inherits the user's Gong permissions; shared context provides organization-wide data. Admin-managed integrations can be disabled or deleted, revoking active tokens. 4. No read-only URL mode, toolset filter, sandbox or regional endpoint was found. Manual/automatic registration and personal/shared authorization are admin configuration options. 5. Private calls are excluded; raw transcripts, message bodies and activity lists are not returned. Docs describe summarized outputs and optional source links. 6. Calls consume Gong credits based on data analyzed; brief cost also depends on open-ended sections. Repeated calls can reanalyze data. No per-call price or rate limit found. 7. MCP schemas were not retrievable. Third-party schema descriptions say date bounds are paired and entity names use exact matching; these details are not established by an official MCP schema. 8. MCP-specific logging, audit trails and telemetry were not found in reviewed docs. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, reporting or upsell tool appears in the complete official tool list. 10. Official docs give tool-selection instructions; these are agent guidance, not documented server-enforced rules. No MCP-delivered skill tool found. 11. No evidence that past agent behavior changes later outputs or tool availability. 12. Flat documented tool set; Gong's separate MCP client is a different feature. 13. No raw API, SQL, script or arbitrary-request tool appears in the official list.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: Gong's official tool list is https://help.gong.io/docs/about-gong-mcp-server and names 3 tools; no official total beyond that list is stated. No catalogue-only tools were added. APIs.io, mcpyet and MartechDB also report these 3 names. mcpmetrics could not read the auth-gated tool list. Manufact lists get_transcript, but that conflicts with Gong's explicit statement that raw transcripts are not returned; it is excluded and recorded in contradictions. Parameter details are not published by Gong; where populated, they are labelled as third-party Agent Discoverability schema evidence.

actions.description: Answers a focused natural-language question about one account using related calls and emails.
actions.parameters: [THIRD-PARTY Agent Discoverability, 2026-10] workspace: string (optional); crmAccount: string (required); question: string (required); fromDateTime: ISO 8601 string (optional); toDateTime: ISO 8601 string (optional); includeSources: boolean (optional, default false). Date bounds are supplied together.

actions.description: Answers a focused natural-language question about one deal using related calls and emails.
actions.parameters: [THIRD-PARTY Agent Discoverability, 2026-10] workspace: string (optional); crmDeal: string (required); question: string (required); fromDateTime: ISO 8601 string (optional); toDateTime: ISO 8601 string (optional); includeSources: boolean (optional, default false). Date bounds are supplied together.

actions.description: Generates a structured multi-category brief for an account, deal or contact.
actions.parameters: [THIRD-PARTY Agent Discoverability, 2026-10] workspace: string (optional); briefName: string (required); entityType: enum ACCOUNT/DEAL/CONTACT (required); crmEntity: string (required); periodType: enum CUSTOM_RANGE/LAST_7DAYS/LAST_30DAYS/LAST_90DAYS (optional, default LAST_90DAYS); fromDateTime: ISO 8601 string (optional); toDateTime: ISO 8601 string (optional); includeSources: boolean (optional, default false). Contacts require CRM ID.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Through this MCP server, agents cannot create, update or delete Gong or CRM data; retrieve raw call transcripts, message bodies or activity lists; or access private calls. Gong's broader platform and APIs provide other features, but this review did not enumerate all human-accessible functionality. https://help.gong.io/docs/about-gong-mcp-server

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Gong recommends concise, insight-oriented questions for ask tools and recommends generate_brief for multi-category summaries. It says to narrow date ranges, use the narrowest entity scope and batch related questions to reduce repeated analysis and credit use. These are recommendations to the client/agent; no enforcement mechanism is documented. Example quote: “Set clear instructions for the agent to batch related questions by entity.”
F_documentation.governance_promises: Gong states: “The MCP server is read-only and does not create, update, or delete data in Gong or the CRM.” It also states: “Private calls are excluded from all results.” It says personal access is limited to data the user is already permitted to view; shared access is organization-wide. The privacy policy says Gong processes customer data on the customer's behalf and under its instructions, subject to the data processing addendum.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The MCP server returns AI-generated insights and summaries rather than raw call transcripts, message bodies or activity lists. With includeSources enabled, it can return links to the calls and emails used.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The read-only behavior and exclusion of private calls are documented claims, but deployed code could not be inspected. Personal-versus-shared access and token revocation are described in the integration administration docs. Credit consumption is documented. No publicly inspectable enforcement, audit, logging or telemetry details were found.

contradictions: OAuth protected-resource metadata advertises both mcp:read and mcp:write, while Gong's official documentation describes the MCP server as read-only and says it does not create, update or delete data. The advertised write scope does not establish that write tools are available.
Manufact lists get_transcript for Gong, but Gong's official documentation says raw data such as call transcripts is not returned. The catalogue-only tool is therefore excluded from actions.
observations_for_research: Gong documents both personal authorization, which follows each user's existing visibility, and shared authorization, where connected users receive organization-wide data access.

Agent-facing docs recommend which tool to select for targeted questions versus structured briefs, while credit consumption increases with analyzed conversation volume, repeated requests and open-ended brief sections.
includeSources defaults to false in the official docs; source links can be included when requested.
notes: Checked links.json, links_check.txt, all prepared official documentation and catalogue pages, OAuth metadata, pricing and legal pages, and code/GITHUB_COMMITS.txt. No official source repository was listed. The hosted endpoint and /install returned HTTP 401. Official docs establish names and high-level behavior but not live schemas, annotations, initialize instructions or protocol version. Detailed parameter notes in actions.json come from the third-party Agent Discoverability page and were not verified against the authenticated endpoint. Third-party catalogues were used only for cross-checking and schema context; Manufact's get_transcript was rejected against Gong's explicit raw-transcript exclusion.
